Helps Pennsylvania households pay for home heating with a once-a-season grant (LIHEAP Cash, 2026-27 season).

LIHEAP Cash is a grant that helps households pay for home heating during the winter season. This benefit checks the main rules for the 2026-27 season: the household lives in Pennsylvania, its income is at or below 150% of the federal poverty guidelines, it is responsible for its primary heating costs, someone in it is a U.S. citizen or lawfully admitted non-citizen, and it has not already received a Cash grant this season.

**Administered by:** [Pennsylvania Department of Human Services, through the County Assistance Offices](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dhs/resources/liheap)

**Program year:** 2026-27 season, November 2, 2026 to April 23, 2027

## Checks

Eligible when every check passes.

- **Lives in pennsylvania**: LIHEAP Cash is for households that permanently live in Pennsylvania (601.31(3)). (`LivesInPennsylvaniaService`)
- **Income at or below 150 percent fpl**: Household income must be equal to or less than 150% of the federal poverty guidelines (601.81 to 601.84). (`HouseholdIncomeWithinPovertyGuidelinesService`)
- **Pays primary heating costs**: The household must be responsible for its primary heating costs. Households whose heat is included in rent based on their income are not eligible (601.31(2)). (`PaysPrimaryHeatingCostsService`)
- **Has citizen or eligible noncitizen**: Someone in the household must be a U.S. citizen or a lawfully admitted non-citizen (601.31(4)). (`HouseholdHasCitizenOrEligibleNoncitizenService`)
- **Not already enrolled**: A household can receive one Cash grant per season (601.43). (`PersonNotEnrolledInBenefitService`)

## Limitations

- Living arrangements that make a household ineligible are not checked: temporary stays, institutions, dorms, fraternity or sorority houses, boarding homes, incarceration, and fleeing felons.
- Heating equipment that is not installed or operating to code is not checked, and neither are the rules for recreational vehicles and home businesses.
- Household size and income are taken as given. LIHEAP leaves ineligible non-citizens, and people who already got Cash in another household, out of household size but still counts their income.
- The applicant may choose the prior month or the prior 12 months as the income period. The screener does not compare the two.
- DHS may change the season dates, and the funds can run out before the season closes.
- Income limits change each February, when DHS adopts the new federal poverty guidelines.

Reduces the taxable assessed value of an owner-occupied primary residence in Philadelphia.

The Homestead Exemption lowers the assessed value of a Philadelphia home by $100,000 before Real Estate Tax is calculated, which saves most homeowners up to $1,399 a year. It is for people who own the home and live in it as their primary residence. Having a mortgage, being a new owner or owing back taxes does not stop someone from qualifying, but a home with a 10-year residential tax abatement cannot get the exemption until the abatement ends or is cancelled.

**Administered by:** [City of Philadelphia Department of Revenue](https://www.phila.gov/departments/department-of-revenue/)

## Checks

Eligible when every check passes.

- **Not already on homestead**: A home gets the exemption once; people who already have it do not need to apply. (`PersonNotEnrolledInBenefitService`)
- **No ten year tax abatement**: Properties with a 10-year residential tax abatement are not eligible until the abatement expires or is cancelled. (`NoTenYearTaxAbatementService`)
- **Owner occupant**: The applicant must own the home and live in it as their primary residence. (`OwnerOccupantService`)
- **Lives in philadelphia pa**: The exemption applies to Philadelphia Real Estate Tax, so the home must be in Philadelphia. (`LivesInPhiladelphiaPaService`)

## Limitations

- Does not check the conditional exemption for people whose name is not on the deed, such as heirs, victims of deed fraud or rent-to-own buyers.
- A home with an active 10-year abatement fails, even though the owner could cancel the abatement and then qualify. A cancelled abatement cannot be restored.
- Does not check whether the person is enrolled in LOOP. LOOP and the Homestead Exemption cannot be held at the same time.
- Ownership, residence and abatement status are taken from the screener answers and are not looked up in City records.

## Sources

- [Get the Homestead Exemption (City of Philadelphia)](https://www.phila.gov/services/payments-assistance-taxes/taxes/property-and-real-estate-taxes/get-real-estate-tax-relief/get-the-homestead-exemption/) (checked November 19, 2026)

post.description:
Philadelphia Longtime Owner Occupants Program (LOOP) for new applicants. Homestead recipients can qualify but must remove that exemption when they enroll; historical owner/close-relative abatements are excluded.

The Longtime Owner Occupants Program (LOOP) limits how much the assessed value of a long-held Philadelphia home can rise for Real Estate Tax. It is for people who have owned and lived in their home for at least 10 years, whose assessment rose at least 50% in one year or 75% over five years, whose taxes are current or in a payment plan, and whose household income is below 120% of area median income for their family size. Someone who received a tax abatement on the property, or whose close relative received one as a previous owner, cannot enroll. A homeowner with the Homestead Exemption can enroll but must have the Homestead Exemption removed.

**Administered by:** [City of Philadelphia Department of Revenue](https://www.phila.gov/departments/department-of-revenue/)

## Checks

Eligible when every check passes.

- **Not already enrolled**: People already in LOOP do not need to apply again. (`PersonNotEnrolledInBenefitService`)
- **Owner occupant**: The applicant must own the home and live in it as their primary residence. (`OwnerOccupantService`)
- **Lives in philadelphia pa**: LOOP applies to Philadelphia Real Estate Tax, so the home must be in Philadelphia. (`LivesInPhiladelphiaPaService`)
- **Ten years owner occupant**: The applicant must have lived in the home for at least 10 years. (`MinYearsOwnerOccupantService`)
- **Assessment increase**: The assessment must have risen at least 50% from last year or at least 75% over the past five years. (`PropertyAssessmentIncreaseService`)
- **Taxes current or payment plan**: Property taxes must be current, or covered by an Owner-Occupied Payment Agreement or an installment plan. (`PropertyTaxesCurrentOrPaymentPlanService`)
- **Meets income requirement**: Household income must be below 120% of area median income for the family size. (`LoopIncomeService`)
- **No disqualifying tax abatement**: No one can enroll who received a tax abatement on the property as its current owner, or whose close relative received one as a previous owner. (`NoDisqualifyingTaxAbatementService`)

## Limitations

- Applies only the 120% of area median income limit for new applicants. Households enrolled before 2023 may stay in the program under the 150% limit, which is not checked.
- The income table covers households of 1 to 10 people. Larger households get no result.
- Assessment values are taken as given and should be the values before any Homestead reduction.
- Whether a past abatement was received by the owner or a close relative is taken from the screener answer.
- Does not remove or check the Homestead Exemption. A Homestead recipient who enrolls in LOOP must ask to have the exemption removed.
- The program has a yearly savings cap ($35 million as of 2023). Enrollment stays open after the cap is reached.

## Sources

- [Apply for the Longtime Owner Occupants Program (LOOP) (City of Philadelphia)](https://www.phila.gov/services/payments-assistance-taxes/payment-plans-and-assistance-programs/income-based-programs-for-residents/apply-for-the-longtime-owner-occupants-program-loop/) (checked November 19, 2026)

Philadelphia Low-Income Real Estate Tax Freeze for owner-occupants whose income plus any spouse's income meets the single/married gross annual limits.

The Low-Income Real Estate Tax Freeze keeps a Philadelphia homeowner's Real Estate Tax from going up, even if the property assessment or tax rate rises. It is for people who own and live in their home as their primary residence and whose total yearly gross income is no more than $33,500 for a single person or $41,500 for a married couple. There is no age requirement.

**Administered by:** [City of Philadelphia Department of Revenue](https://www.phila.gov/departments/department-of-revenue/)

## Checks

Eligible when every check passes.

- **Not already enrolled**: People who already have the freeze do not need to apply again. (`PersonNotEnrolledInBenefitService`)
- **Owner occupant**: The applicant must own the home and live in it as their primary residence. (`OwnerOccupantService`)
- **Lives in philadelphia pa**: The freeze applies to Philadelphia Real Estate Tax, so the home must be in Philadelphia. (`LivesInPhiladelphiaPaService`)
- **Meets income requirement**: Total yearly gross income must be no more than $33,500 for a single person or $41,500 for a married couple. (`TaxFreezeIncomeService`)

## Limitations

- The combined gross income of the applicant and spouse is taken as given. The City decides which income counts from the documents submitted.
- The married limit applies whenever the screener lists a spouse for the applicant, wherever the spouse lives.
- The income limits are those on the City page when it was checked; the City may change them.
- Ownership and residence are taken from the screener answers and are not looked up in City records.

A Philadelphia property-tax payment agreement for eligible owner occupants.

An Owner-Occupied Real Estate Tax Payment Agreement (OOPA) lets a Philadelphia homeowner who is behind on Real Estate Tax pay the past-due balance in monthly installments based on household income, with no down payment. It is for people who live in the home they own and owe past-due property tax.

**Administered by:** [City of Philadelphia Department of Revenue](https://www.phila.gov/departments/department-of-revenue/)

## Checks

Eligible when every check passes.

- **Not already on owner occupied payment agreement**: People who already have an OOPA do not need to apply again. (`PersonNotEnrolledInBenefitService`)
- **Lives in philadelphia pa**: The agreement covers Philadelphia Real Estate Tax, so the home must be in Philadelphia. (`LivesInPhiladelphiaPaService`)
- **Owner occupant**: The applicant must live in the home they own. (`OwnerOccupantService`)
- **Tax delinquent**: The agreement is a way to pay Real Estate Tax that is past due, so there must be a past-due balance. (`TaxDelinquentService`)

## Limitations

- Does not work out the monthly payment, which depends on household income and size.
- Does not check whether a trust or a person with a legal interest but not on the deed can qualify; the City reviews those cases.
- Whether taxes are past due is taken from the screener answer, not from City records.
- Ownership and residence are taken from the screener answers and are not looked up in City records.

Freezes Philadelphia real estate taxes for qualifying older homeowners.

The Low-Income Senior Citizen Real Estate Tax Freeze keeps an older Philadelphia homeowner's Real Estate Tax from going up, even if the property assessment or tax rate rises. It is for people who own and live in their home and who are 65 or older, live with a spouse who is 65 or older, or are 50 or older and the widow or widower of someone who reached 65. The City also sets an income limit: $33,500 for a single person or $41,500 for a married couple.

**Administered by:** [City of Philadelphia Department of Revenue](https://www.phila.gov/departments/department-of-revenue/)

## Checks

Eligible when every check passes.

- **Not already on senior citizen tax freeze**: People who already have the freeze do not need to apply again. (`PersonNotEnrolledInBenefitService`)
- **Owner occupant**: The applicant must own the home and live in it as their primary residence. (`OwnerOccupantService`)
- **Lives in philadelphia pa**: The freeze applies to Philadelphia Real Estate Tax, so the home must be in Philadelphia. (`LivesInPhiladelphiaPaService`)
- **Meets age requirement**: The applicant must be 65 or older, have a spouse who is 65 or older, or be 50 or older and widowed from someone who reached 65. (`SctfAgeRequirementService`)

## Limitations

- Does not check the income limit of $33,500 for a single person or $41,500 for a married couple. A household over the limit can show as eligible.
- Ages are measured on December 31 of the current year, so someone who turns 65 (or 50) later this year already shows as eligible.
- Does not check that a spouse aged 65 or older lives in the same household.
- Whether a late spouse reached 65 is taken from the screener answer.
- Ownership and residence are taken from the screener answers and are not looked up in City records.

post.description:
Checks that annual household income is at or below a percentage of the HHS poverty guidelines for the household's size.

Finds the HHS poverty guideline for the household's size, multiplies it by the given percent, and passes when annual household income is equal to or less than the result. For 2026 the guideline is $15,960 for one person plus $5,680 for each additional person, so 150% is $23,940 for one person plus $8,520 for each additional person. Returns no result when income or household size is missing or invalid, or when the guideline year is not available.

## Parameters

- `percent` (number): Percentage of the poverty guideline to use as the income limit, for example 150 for 150%.
- `guidelineYear` (number): Year of the HHS poverty guidelines to use, for example 2026.

## Limitations

- Only the 2026 guidelines are available. Any other guideline year returns no result.
- Uses the guidelines for the 48 contiguous states and DC, not those for Alaska or Hawaii.
- Takes household income and size as given. It does not decide whose income counts, which income is excluded, or how pay is annualized.
- Does not round the limit. A program that publishes rounded limits may differ by a few dollars.

## Sources

- [Pennsylvania LIHEAP FFY 2027 Final State Plan](https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/dhs/documents/services/assistance/documents/heating-assistance_liheap/2027-liheap-state-plan.pdf): Income eligibility: 150% of the 2026 federal poverty guidelines, by household size (checked November 12, 2026)

Last reviewed November 12, 2026.

x-bdt-reference.explanation: Passes when the screener answer says the property has an active 10-year residential tax abatement, and fails when it says it does not. Returns no result when the answer is missing.
limitations: Relies on the screener answer. It does not look up or verify records.
Only active abatements count. Past abatements that have ended do not.
